Length: Full tentacle length in world units, measured from each root point outward. Audio band4 modulates it.
Grow: Growth amount, 0-1. Multiplies Length: 0 = tentacles retracted (hidden), 1 = fully grown.
Autogrow: On: tentacles continuously grow and retract over time, overriding the manual Grow value.
Speed: Animation speed multiplier for wiggle, wave and pulse motion (which run on absolute time). 0 = frozen.
Seed: Random seed. Changing it gives each tentacle a different phase and shape.
Segments: Rings along each tentacle. Higher = smoother curves, heavier mesh. Cost scales with points x Segments x Sides.
Sides: Vertices around each tube. Higher = rounder, heavier mesh.
Thickness: Tentacle radius at the root, in world units.
Taper: Exponent of the thinning toward the tip. 0 = constant radius; 1 = linear; higher = stays thick longer then thins sharply.
Tipmin: Minimum tip thickness as a fraction of Thickness (0-1), so tentacles do not end in a needle point.
Wiggle: Strength of the noise-driven writhing of the spine, relative to length. 0 = straight radial tubes. Audio band1 adds to it.
Noisefreq: How fast the writhing noise varies along the tentacle. Higher = more kinks and curls.
Wave: Amplitude of the sideways travelling sway, relative to length. 0 = off. Audio band3 modulates it.
Wavefreq: Number of sway waves along a tentacle. Higher = tighter S-curves.
Pulse: Strength of the thickness pulses travelling along the tentacle (0-1 fraction of the radius). 0 = off. Beat swells thickness.
Pulsefreq: Frequency of the thickness pulses along the tentacle. Higher = more bulges per tentacle.
Resolution: Preview TOP size in pixels. Only affects the node viewer preview.
Roughness: Preview material roughness, 0 = mirror-like, 1 = fully diffuse.
Envintensity: Brightness of the preview's environment lighting and reflections. 0 = none.
Redaccent: Strength of the red rim accent light in the preview. 0 = off.
Camdist: Preview camera distance from the origin in world units.
Camheight: Preview camera height above the origin in world units.
